headline: eBay's Q1 GMV jumped 14% FX-neutral on sports cards and a bullion bump; eBay raised its 2026 GMV outlook.
guidance_note: FY26 FX-neutral GMV growth raised to 7-7.5% (ex-Depop); Q2 GMV $21.3-21.7bn (+8-10%), rev $2.97-3.03bn, EPS $1.46-1.51.
key_messages: GMV $22.2bn, +18% reported / +14% FX-neutral; revenue +19% reported / +17% FX-neutral.
US GMV up ~27% per call summaries; international grew just over 2% organic FX-neutral, so the gap with the US is wide.
Active buyers 136M, +1% YoY (135M ex-Tise); US active buyers +6%, enthusiast buyers +8%.
Sports trading cards outpaced the Pokemon 30th anniversary as a driver; gold/silver bullion gave a transitory boost.
Management guided Q2 slower as bullion volume reverts to normal.

consumer.big_ticket: Collectibles/hobby spend accelerated; precious-metals buying (bullion) temporarily lifted GMV.

macro_read: Hobbyist and precious-metals buying lifted eBay's results, which reflects asset-price and enthusiast demand more than broad consumer health. Buyer growth stayed near flat.
notes: Bullion boost was flagged as transitory; it drives most of the guided Q1-to-Q2 slowdown.
Big FX tailwind: reported GMV growth (18%) well above FX-neutral (14%).
US GMV +27% figure comes from call summaries; its exact definition is unconfirmed.
EPS consensus is Zacks ($1.66 beat by 5.06%); some auto-generated sites cite $1.61. Revenue consensus is Zacks' post-report figure; its pre-report figure was $3.02bn.
Stock reaction: sources conflict (+3.36% vs -1.24%), so left null.
No tariff/de minimis commentary found for this call.
